pages.text: Library About RUA Library Library Services Resources & Research News & Events Contact Library The Library at the Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) is a key resource center that supports academic learning, research, and extension activities in agriculture and related disciplines. It is a central hub for students, faculty, and researchers, providing access to a wealth of information essential for the development of Cambodia's agricultural sector. RUA Library: Comprehensive Collection: The library holds an extensive collection of books, journals, theses, dissertations, research papers, and periodicals, focusing on agriculture, agronomy, animal science, forestry, fisheries, food technology, agricultural economics, and environmental sciences. It also includes resources on general education subjects, science, and technology, contributing to the broader knowledge base of the university community. Digital Resources: In addition to print materials, the library offers access to a wide range of digital resources, including e-books, online databases, academic journals, and research publications. Students and faculty can access databases such as AGORA, HINARI, and JSTOR, which provide information on agricultural science, health, and environmental research. Research Support: The RUA Library is committed to supporting academic and scientific research. It provides guidance on literature reviews, research methodologies, citation management, and academic writing. Librarians are available to assist with information retrieval, database searches, and finding specific resources relevant to research projects. Study Spaces and Facilities: The library provides a quiet and comfortable environment for study, equipped with reading rooms, individual study desks, group study areas, and discussion rooms. It also offers access to computers, printers, and internet facilities, allowing students and researchers to access online resources and conduct research efficiently. Special Collections and Archives: The library houses special collections that include rare books, historical documents, and publications related to Cambodian agriculture and rural development. It maintains archives of research projects, agricultural studies, and significant works by RUA faculty, serving as a repository of the university’s scholarly output. Library Services: Borrowing and Lending : Students, faculty, and staff can borrow books and other materials using their university ID cards. Reference Services : Librarians provide assistance with finding information, locating resources, and accessing reference materials. Interlibrary Loan : The library offers an interlibrary loan service, allowing users to access materials from partner libraries and institutions if needed. Workshops and Training : The library regularly organizes workshops and training sessions on information literacy, research skills, citation tools, and effective use of digital resources. Online Catalog and OPAC: The library has an Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) , enabling students and faculty to search the library’s collection, check availability, and reserve books online. The catalog is accessible both on-campus and remotely, making it easier to locate materials and plan research effectively. Collaboration and Partnerships: The RUA Library collaborates with other universities, research institutions, and agricultural organizations in Cambodia and internationally, facilitating resource sharing, joint research, and access to a wider range of academic materials. It also participates in library networks and consortia to expand access to information and improve library services. Mission and Vision of the RUA Library: Mission : To provide comprehensive information resources and services that support the educational, research, and extension objectives of the Royal University of Agriculture. Vision : To be a leading agricultural library in Cambodia, fostering knowledge, research, and innovation in sustainable agriculture and related fields. Library Environment: The RUA Library aims to create a welcoming and inclusive space for learning and knowledge sharing. It encourages collaborative study while also maintaining designated quiet zones for focused academic work. The library frequently updates its resources to keep pace with advancements in agricultural science, technology, and best practices, ensuring that users have access to current and relevant information.
